title: Cannot build --with-secure-transport from source macOS 14.4
body: I downloaded curl 8.6.0 on macOS 14.4 and ran `sudo autoreconf -fi`, `sudo ./configure --with-secure-transport`, `make`, and `sudo make install`. This used to work before recent OS updates, but configure now says `select TLS backend(s) or disable TLS with --without-ssl`, even though I selected Secure Transport. The build does not complete, so `curl` remains at version 8.5.0 instead of upgrading.

symptoms_visible: Running configure with `--with-secure-transport` reports that I must select a TLS backend, and the build stops before curl can be upgraded from 8.5.0.
N0.label: N0 Secure Transport configure failure reported

symptoms_visible: Configure still reports that no TLS backend was selected even though I passed `--with-secure-transport`.
N1.label: N1 partial config log collected

symptoms_visible: The daily snapshot's configure script enables Secure Transport on the machine I tested, while my original build attempt still leaves the installed curl at 8.5.0.
N2.label: N2 snapshot succeeds on test machine

symptoms_visible: On the ordinary Macs in my organization, configure still stops with the message that no TLS backend was selected.
The machine where the snapshot configured successfully was a nonrepresentative test machine with manually installed tools.
N2_x.label: N2_x Autotools-only explanation rejected

symptoms_visible: On the vanilla organization Macs, both the normal release configure script and the snapshot configure script report the same missing-TLS-backend error, while the earlier curl 8.5 installation workflow had worked.
N3.label: N3 failure scope clarified across shipped scripts

symptoms_visible: I had more than ten users run the same script with curl 8.7.1, and they updated successfully without the TLS-backend selection error.
N_terminal.label: terminal current release builds successfully

question_patterns: Can you inspect config.log and paste the portion around the failure, searching backward for relevant errors?
What does config.log show before configure reports that no TLS backend was selected?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The block I found shows Apple clang 15 targeting arm64-apple-darwin23.4.0. The `gcc -V`, `-qversion`, and `-version` probes print unsupported-option errors, but the following checks say the C compiler works, produce `a.out`, run the test program, and compile object files successfully. I did not see this block in the output before.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: My log says `--with-secure-transport` is an unrecognized configure option and never records that argument.
I see the same compiler checks with a slightly newer Apple clang build number.

edges.comment: Reporter c4, answering participant1 c3. This is only the reporter's partial config.log output; participant3 later notes in c36 that the excerpt does not contain the relevant failure and asks for the complete file, which the reporter never supplies.

question_patterns: Can you try the configure script from a daily snapshot and report whether it accepts Secure Transport?
Please run the daily snapshot's shipped configure script with the same option and paste its configuration summary.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On the machine I used for this test, the daily snapshot configured successfully. Its summary says host `aarch64-apple-darwin23.4.0`, curl `8.7.0-20240314`, and `SSL: enabled (Secure Transport)`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The daily snapshot fails on this same test machine with exactly the same message that no TLS backend was selected.
The snapshot configures Secure Transport successfully but reports a different snapshot date.

edges.comment: Reporter c12-c13, after participant1 c8-c11 requested a daily-snapshot probe. The successful summary is raw measurement output. The reporter also volunteered Autoconf 2.71, Automake 1.16.5, and Libtool 2.4.7 from this test machine.

solution.intent: Conclude that the locally installed Autotools setup generated a broken configure script, then bisect or replace those tools and compare the generated script with the working snapshot script.
solution.concrete_example: Because the snapshot configure script worked, compare it with the locally generated configure script around the TLS-library check, bisect the Autoconf, Automake, and Libtool setup, or ask the Autotools maintainers why the generated shell logic is broken.

edges.comment: Participant1 c14-c18 attributed the discrepancy to the reporter's Autotools installation after the snapshot worked on one machine. Reporter c19, c22, c26, and c28 then explained that this was a nonrepresentative test machine and that the ordinary organization Macs lacked those tools yet still failed with shipped configure scripts. This brush-off diagnosis did not explain the affected fleet.

question_patterns: On an ordinary affected Mac, what happens when you run the configure script shipped in the release rather than generating one yourself?
Please clarify separately whether the release configure script and the snapshot configure script work on the vanilla affected Macs.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On the ordinary Macs, configure is not working from either the normal 8.6.0 release or the snapshot. Both fail with the same TLS-selection error. Please disregard my earlier report that the snapshot worked because that test was on the special machine.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The shipped release and snapshot configure scripts work on every vanilla Mac; only the script regenerated on my test machine fails.
The same failure occurs on a smaller subset of otherwise equivalent organization Macs.

edges.comment: Reporter c19-c30, in response to participant1 c21-c29. The reporter retracts the earlier generalization from the test machine and states that both shipped release and snapshot configure scripts fail on ordinary organization Macs. In c32 the reporter also volunteers that the earlier curl 8.5 installation had worked across the fleet.

solution.intent: Treat the precise cause as unresolved and specific to the affected environment or invocation rather than claim a demonstrated curl source defect; retry with the current release, verify on affected machines, and collect a complete config.log plus shell-level tracing if the failure recurs.
solution.concrete_example: Do not switch between OpenSSL and LibreSSL to address this check: selecting Secure Transport is sufficient and independent of those libraries. Retry the current curl source release on representative affected Macs. In the thread, more than ten users subsequently ran the same script with 8.7.1 successfully. If the error returns, preserve the complete config.log and add diagnostic shell output around configure's argument handling and TLS-selection variable instead of assuming a known curl fix.
solution.inference_hint: The maintainers established that Secure Transport selection does not consult OpenSSL or LibreSSL, shipped configure scripts do not use installed Autotools, the relevant TLS-selection check was effectively unchanged from the previously working release, and other macOS systems and CI built successfully. Those facts support an environment- or invocation-specific failure, but the complete log and requested tracing were never supplied, so the exact culprit and any curl-side fix remain unknown. The later successful update is verification, not proof that a particular curl bug was fixed.

edges.comment: Participant1 c27 and c31-c35 explains why installed Autotools and unrelated TLS libraries cannot control this shipped configure check, notes successful macOS and CI builds, and recommends tracing the plain shell logic. Participant3 c36 requests the complete config.log, but it is never posted. Reporter c37 then relays successful use of the same script by more than ten affected users with 8.7.1; these affected organization users are folded into the simulated user side. Participant1 c38 closes with 'Works'. No concrete curl defect, patch, or root-cause mechanism was identified.

satisfaction_conditions: Must state the final accepted diagnosis accurately: no specific curl source defect or fixed mechanism was established; the evidence points to an unidentified condition in the affected organization's environment or invocation.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: the contradictory snapshot results came from different machines, shipped release and snapshot scripts both failed on representative Macs, while other macOS builders and curl CI successfully selected Secure Transport.
Must not blame the presence or absence of OpenSSL or LibreSSL, because selecting Secure Transport does not depend on either library.

Must not settle on a broken locally installed Autotools setup as the complete explanation: representative affected Macs failed with shipped configure scripts, and running a shipped configure script does not use installed Autotools.
Must not claim that a known curl bug was fixed in the later release; the thread identified no patch or mechanism, only that the same script subsequently succeeded for more than ten affected users.

Must ask for verification on representative affected machines before declaring resolution; if the failure recurs, request the complete config.log and trace the configure shell logic around option handling and TLS selection.

persona_hint.experience_level: Organization administrator and scripting user with moderate command-line experience. Can build software, report tool versions, and deploy an update script across hundreds of Macs, but is unfamiliar with the distinction between generated configure scripts, shipped configure scripts, and when Autotools participates.
persona_hint.communication_style: Persistent and direct, with detailed pasted outputs and fleet context. Sometimes revises earlier claims after realizing a test machine was not representative, and asks for explicit debugging steps rather than broad diagnostic advice.
